brave.snippet:
Nvidia Corporation (/ɛnˈvɪdiə/ en-VID-ee-ə) is an American multinational technology company headquartered in Santa Clara, California. The company develops graphics processing units (GPUs), systems on chips (SoCs), and application programming interfaces (APIs) for gaming, data science, high-performance computing, artificial intelligence (AI) hardware, and mobile and automotive applications. Founded in 1993 by Jensen Huang, Chris Malachowsky, and Curtis Priem, Nvidia is among the largest companies by market capitalization.
Nvidia was founded on April 5, 1993, by Jensen Huang, a Taiwanese-American electrical engineer who was previously the director of CoreWare at LSI Logic and a microprocessor designer at AMD, Chris Malachowsky, an engineer who worked at Sun Microsystems, and Curtis Priem, who was previously a senior staff engineer and graphics chip designer at IBM and Sun Microsystems.
In early 1993, the three founders began working together on their new startup in Priem's townhouse in Fremont, California. With $40,000 in the bank (equivalent to $89,000 in 2025), the company was born. The company subsequently received $20 million of venture capital funding from Sequoia Capital, Sutter Hill Ventures, and others. During the late 1990s, Nvidia was one of 70 startup companies pursuing the idea that graphics acceleration for video games was the path to the future.
Nvidia initially had no name. Priem's first idea was "Primal Graphics", a syllabic abbreviation of two of the founders' last names, but that left out Huang. They soon discovered it was impossible to create a workable name with syllables from all three founders' names, after considering "Huaprimal", "Prihuamal", "Malluapri", etc.

ceramic.title: Nvidia GeForce RTX 5090 review: the ultimate DLSS 4 billboard | Rock Paper Shotgun
ceramic.snippet:
Nvidia GeForce RTX 5090 review: the ultimate DLSS 4 billboard | Rock Paper Shotgun

  There’s definitely a sense of Nvidia going \"Sod it\" with this one, cutting the sensibility brakes to produce something that even hyperenthusiasts might find a bit too mad. Besides the price, this is by far the biggest PSU-muncher to ever wear a GeForce badge: the Founders Edition I tested demands a thundering 1000W power supply and is rated to hoover up to 575W at once, a threat that it made good on by pulling 578W in Cyberpunk 2077 . In comparison, the 450W-rated RTX 4090 looks like it can be powered by potatoes. Credit to the redesigned dual-fan cooler for keeping a lid on temperatures, which I nonetheless measured peaking at a very manageable 74°c.

 Nevertheless, it’s hard to ignore how the jump from the RTX 4090 to the RTX 5090 isn’t nearly as big or as consistent as the former’s improvement over the RTX 3090. Nvidia’s top two GPUs are almost level in Horizon Forbidden West and Assassin’s Creed Mirage , and the differences remain minor once you start adding upscaling. Quality-level DLSS in Forbidden West, for example, got it up to 137fps on the RTX 5090 and 125fps on the RTX 4090: hardly a grand leap forward.

  MFG is also but one part of DLSS 4, which covers a range of tricks that both are and aren’t exclusive to this new Nvidia generation. The RTX 5090 thus also has the duty of showcasing some tech that will benefit GPUs going right back to the RTX 20 series, such as DLSS 4’s new 'Transformer' model and support for 'DLSS overrides' in the Nvidia app .

 Firstly, the Transformer model is a rejigged technique for how DLSS applies its best-in-class anti-aliasing. It runs slightly slower than the preexisting ‘Convolutional Neural Network’ model, averaging 120fps in Cyberpunk 2077 at 4K/Ultra versus the 132fps of the older version.

Nvidia Serial Number Lookup: How To Find Your GPU Serial Number?

  Nvidia serial number is mandatory if you are willing to know the left warranty of your graphics card.  

  You can find your GPU’s serial number on the GPU itself or on its packaging. Also, you can find it on your computer’s display settings or device manager. There is also a command that you can put in the command prompt to find it out. Also, there are apps like GPU-Z and SIW that will find your NVIDIA serial number for you. 

 Nvidia Serial Number Lookup: How To Find The Nvidia Serial Number?   

 There are quite a few methods of finding the Nvidia serial number of your GPU. Check out what they are and which is the most convenient for you. 

 The first place you must look for the serial number is the product packaging. So, remember where you stored your GPU package. Once you find it, the serial number should be on the barcode. 

 This method is easier than the previous two. To do this, right-click on an open space on your screen. Then go to display settings. Scroll down to find  “Advanced Display Settings.” Then go to  “Display Adapter Properties for Display 1” Select  “Properties”. Then go to the details tab. Choose the device instant path from the dropdown menu and it should show you the GPU serial number. 

 You can find the “Device Instant Path” from the device manager too. Search device manager from the Windows search option. Once you find it, find “Display adapters”. Click on it once, then your GPU model number will show up. Right-click on it then select properties. 

 With all the methods we have described above, you should have your GPU serial number. With this serial number, you can check the warranty of your NVIDIA graphic.  

 Now, you will need to reach out to the NVIDIA Customer Service team. But for that, first, you have an NVIDIA account. If you do not have an NVIDIA account, you can open one from their website. Provide all the necessary information to have your account opened.

context.title: Who founded Nvidia? In 1993, three engineers got together at America's iconic Denny's diner and changed the course of tech history
context.snippet:
Nvidia was established in 1993 by Jensen Huang, Chris Malachowsky, and Curtis Priem to improve computer graphics. The company evolved from a focus on graphics chips to becoming a leader in artificial intelligence technology. Jensen Huang has resigned as CEO after leading the company for 33 years, impacting its direction and identity. Colette Kress has been appointed interim CEO while searching for a permanent successor.
He previously worked at Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) and had education in electrical engineering in Oregon State University and Stanford University. Huang became the CEO when the company was founded. Chris Malachowsky was an engineer at Sun Microsystems. His background includes graphics technologies and computer engineering. According to the official Nvidia biography, Chris is referred to as a founder of Nvidia and Nvidia Fellow with many years of experience in core technologies of the company. Also Read | $151 billion fortune, $36 million salary: How Jensen Huang makes his money at Nvidia Curtis Priem was an employee of Sun Microsystems prior to founding Nvidia. Priem became the first chief technology officer at Nvidia and occupied the post from 1993 to 2003. His alma mater, Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute, refers to him for his many contributions in the field of graphics hardware and more than 200 patents. Did Jensen Huang really start Nvidia at Denny's? One of the unique things about Nvidia’s history is an American diner. The three co-founders, Huang, Malachowsky, and Priem met up at a Denny’s restaurant in San Jose, California, in 1993 to plan their graphics-chip startup company. The personal computers would require better hardware capabilities to cope with increasingly complex visuals, they thought. This location was special to Huang as he used to work there during his teenage years. seltz.title: The history of NVIDIA – LinuxPro
seltz.snippet:
In 1993, three engineers met at a Denny's diner in California to found a graphics chip company in a market that already had dozens of competitors. Thirty years later, that company would become — at several points — **the most valuable on the planet**. This is NVIDIA's history: from the flops that nearly killed it to the happy accident called CUDA that put it at the center of the AI revolution.

## 1993: three founders and a diner table

**Jensen Huang** (formerly LSI Logic and AMD), **Chris Malachowsky** and **Curtis Priem** (both formerly Sun Microsystems) founded NVIDIA in April 1993, with US$ 40 thousand and the thesis that video games' 3D graphics would drive the future of computing. Jensen was exactly 30 — and made a commitment he maintains today: he is the semiconductor industry's longest-serving founding CEO.

## 1995–1997: the flop and the rescue

The first product, the **NV1** (1995), was an instructive failure: it bet on quadratic surfaces while the world (and Microsoft's new DirectX) standardized on triangles. The company reached 1996 on the brink of bankruptcy — it laid off more than half its staff and had enough cash for one last gamble. The famous internal motto dates from that period: *“our company is thirty days from going out of business”*. That gamble was the **RIVA 128** (1997), a fast, cheap DirectX chip that sold a million units in four months and saved the company.

## 1999: the birth of the term “GPU”

In October **1999**, months after its IPO, NVIDIA launched the **GeForce 256** and coined the term we still use today: *Graphics Processing Unit*. The real innovation was **hardware T&L** (transformation and lighting), taking work off the CPU. The following year, it bought the remains of the legendary **3dfx** — the rival that defined the Voodoo era — and secured the graphics chip contract for the first **Xbox**.
